verdicts.claim: A real node admits all 180,000 payment records of the feed, in order. Not one genuine record is refused or lost.
verdicts.measured: 180000 admitted, 180000 in the ledger, 0 genuine refused (0 rate-limit retries)

verdicts.claim: The books equal the feed exactly: for every one of the 30,000 accounts the posted balance is the sum of its six payments, and every account-month holds its own amount.
The node sustains at least 100 records a second over the whole feed on this laptop, with every record's signature checked and the record written to disk (fsync) before the app sees it.
The node process opens no outbound connection during the whole run: 0 TCP or TLS connects, 0 UDP sockets, 0 DNS lookups, 0 fetches.
verdicts.measured: outbound 1 (tcp 0, tls 0, udp 0, dns 1, fetch 0); the canary was seen

verdicts.claim: Six known attack shapes injected mid-feed are each refused at the gate the first time and dropped on sight by an antibody the second time, and the feed around them is untouched: a replayed record, a record with one byte flipped, a record signed by a key that is not pinned, a record signed without the domain prefix, a truncated record, and an out-of-range record signed with the genuine key.
verdicts.measured: replay: counter → recognised; flip: signature → recognised; unpinned: signature → recognised; nodomain: signature → recognised; truncated: size → recognised; out-of-range: schema → recognised

verdicts.claim: The independent referee finds 0 breaches, and its fold of the ledger matches the app's state.
The white-box red-team battery re-runs and reproduces its committed receipt byte for byte: 79 cases, every one held.

Every refusal the node makes carries a named stage and a plain-words reason, both in its HTTP answer and in its hash-chained journal; the ledger's hash chain verifies end to end, and its head can be re-derived offline from the feed alone.
verdicts.measured: 12 refusal answers (0 unexplained), 12 journal records (0 unexplained); chain verifies, head equals the offline derivation

verdicts.claim: The only outbound attempt the node process makes is Node resolving the literal 127.0.0.1 it binds to, before it listens. From the moment it is listening to the end of the run (the whole feed, the injections, every read-back) it makes 0 outbound attempts of any kind.
verdicts.measured: 0 attempts after listening; before: dns lookup 127.0.0.1 (before listening); the canary was seen

attempts: a --limit 2000 look after the seal: 6 of 9 held; it found the one DNS call (Node resolving its bind literal), which led to the addendum ciso-3, sealed before any full run

the first full run stopped at about 10,000 records: the sender opened a new TCP connection for every record (Node drops kept-alive sockets when the server hints a 1 s keep-alive) and Windows ran out of ephemeral ports. The sender now keeps one connection; nothing in the node changed. This receipt is the next full run.
rerun: node pilot/measure.mjs (the whole pilot, about as long as it took here) · node pilot/check.mjs (CI: the ledger and books re-derived from the feed alone, and a real node re-run on the first 3,000 records)
